context.summary: Hands-on on claude 2.1.329 (T-claude-adapter probe): a `-p` run with `--settings` registering SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and others wrote no hook records; `--debug-file` shows managed policy skipping non-managed hooks while the organisation's own managed hook ran. The adapter already maps status from the listing alone and uses hook records only when they exist, so it ships as listing-primary; this asks the lead to confirm that reading of D-claude-status-source.

options.tradeoff: Works under any policy. Hook records refine needs_input (tool name, question) when present; without them status comes from the listing only, and needs_input from the listing stays marked "unverified signal" until a probe observes it. Loses the hook-only signals (elicitation, exact permission tool) on locked-down machines.
Keeps D-claude-status-source as written, but Start would have to refuse (or status degrade to unknown) wherever policy blocks hooks, which is common in managed enterprise setups.

data.question: On this machine a managed setting `allowManagedHooksOnly` is on, so command hooks passed with `--settings` never run (debug log: "Skipping plugin hooks - allowManagedHooksOnly is enabled"). D-claude-status-source chose hooks plus listing. Should the adapter treat hooks as an optional enrichment and make `claude agents --json` the primary status source?
data.title: Status source when managed policy blocks --settings hooks
